P0100.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Malfunction
possibleCauses: Fouled or dirty MAF sensor wire
P0100.diagnosticSteps:
1. Inspect intake tubing for loose clamps or tears.
2. Spray clean MAF sensor with dedicated MAF cleaner.
3. Verify 12V power supply and ground to MAF connector.

P0101.title: Mass Air Flow Circuit Range/Performance Problem
P0101.diagnosticSteps:
1. Inspect and replace air filter if clogged.
2. Check live MAF g/s reading on diagnostic scanner at idle (~2-5 g/s for 2.0L engine).

P0133.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
possibleCauses: Exhaust manifold leak upstream of sensor
P0133.diagnosticSteps:
1. Inspect exhaust manifold and downpipe for soot traces/cracks.
2. Monitor live O2 sensor 1 voltage graph for rapid 0.1V to 0.9V switching rate.

P0171.title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
possibleCauses: Weak fuel pump / clogged fuel filter
P0171.diagnosticSteps:
1. Perform smoke test on intake manifold to pinpoint vacuum leaks.
2. Test fuel rail pressure with mechanical gauge.
3. Inspect Short Term & Long Term Fuel Trim values.

P0172.title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
P0172.diagnosticSteps:
1. Inspect fuel pressure regulator for diaphragm leak into vacuum line.
2. Check EVAP purge valve for vacuum pass-through when de-energized.

P0300.title: Random / Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
P0300.diagnosticSteps:
1. CAUTION: Flashing MIL indicates active catalyst damage. Avoid heavy throttle.
2. Check ignition coil power supply and ground harness.
3. Execute cylinder compression test across all cylinders.

P0301.title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
P0301.diagnosticSteps:
1. Swap Cylinder 1 ignition coil to Cylinder 2; clear DTC and check if misfire follows coil.
2. Inspect Cylinder 1 spark plug electrode condition and gap.

P0302.title: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
P0302.diagnosticSteps:
1. Swap Cylinder 2 coil to Cylinder 3; re-test for code shift.
2. Test injector pulse using noid light.

P0420.title: Catalytic Converter System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
possibleCauses: Exhaust leak between upstream and downstream O2 sensors
P0420.diagnosticSteps:
1. Inspect downstream O2 sensor signal (should be steady ~0.45V - 0.7V on healthy cat).
2. Measure exhaust temperature delta at catalytic converter inlet vs outlet with IR thermometer.

P0455.title: EVAP System Gross Leak Detected
possibleCauses: Loose, damaged, or missing gas cap
P0455.diagnosticSteps:
1. Inspect gas cap rubber seal for cracks or debris.
2. Command EVAP vent solenoid closed with scan tool and apply low-pressure smoke test to EVAP service port.

P0700.title: Transmission Control System Malfunction (MIL Request)
symptoms: Transmission in Limp Mode (3rd gear lockup)
possibleCauses: Sub-module fault in Transmission Control Module (TCM)
P0700.diagnosticSteps:
1. Scan TCM module specifically for secondary transmission P-codes (e.g. P0750, P0755).
2. Verify fluid level, color, and smell.

B0001.title: Driver Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control Malfunction
possibleCauses: Corroded airbag harness connector under column
B0001.diagnosticSteps:
1. Disconnect vehicle battery and wait 10 minutes before servicing SRS.
2. Inspect steering wheel clock spring harness for continuity.

C0035.title: Left Front Wheel Speed Circuit Malfunction
possibleCauses: Damaged ABS wheel speed sensor cable
C0035.diagnosticSteps:
1. Inspect wiring harness near LF wheel well for chaffing or hub movement damage.
2. Measure AC voltage output from sensor while spinning wheel manually.

U0100.title: Lost Communication With ECM / PCM 'A'
symptoms: Dashboard instrument cluster warning lights illuminated
Scantool cannot establish link to ECM
possibleCauses: High-speed CAN bus line shorted to ground or power
U0100.diagnosticSteps:
1. Check main ECM fuses and power relay under hood fuse box.
2. Measure resistance across CAN High (pin 6) and CAN Low (pin 14) at OBD-II connector (should read ~60 ohms).
